content:
maya: rolling Neutrino-8B (int4) into canary cluster now. initial perf looked good, but load test showed weird tiny frees + a single OOM on one host.
ryan: which host and what pattern? paste the short log snippet if you have it.
maya: g-ml-12. pattern was lots of small allocs then a sudden device OOM at step ~3200. excerpt:
```
[2026-03-18 14:22:11] OOM @ step 3203 on g-ml-12
small alloc churn: 16k/32k blocks from prefetch + kv updates
vmem_peak: 40.4G, device_reserved: 41.6G, free_end: 180MB
```
sasha: smells like fragmentation from prefetch + KV writes. did the canary enable prefetch by default?
maya: yes, model-catalog default had prefetch: true to optimize cold starts.
ryan: prefetch often reduces tail-latency but it can fragment int4 allocations because of alignment padding. we hit similar constraints with aether18b. my quick hypothesis: prefetch=true + high max_concurrent -> many short-lived small buffers that don't compact well.
elaine: what experiments have you run?
maya: ran controlled load on g-ml-12: 
- config A: prefetch=true, max_concurrent=12, max_new_tokens=512 -> 4/10 OOMs
- config B: prefetch=false, max_concurrent=6, max_new_tokens=256 -> 0/10 OOMs, p95 latency increased ~15%
ryan: ok. tradeoff is latency vs reliability. given canary SLO of p95 < 450ms, +15% still fits. throughput dropped ~18% though.
sasha: also tried adjusting kv_eviction_policy to "aggressive" vs "conservative":
- aggressive removed hot KV quickly, reduced peak but increased re-fetches
- conservative kept KV longer, reduced churn and fragmentation
recommend conservative for onboarding.
maya: made a local config change and re-ran: prefetch=false + kv_eviction_policy=conservative + max_concurrent=6. no OOMs in 50 runs.
ryan: nice. operationally we should: 1) lower default max_new_tokens for int4 canaries (256), 2) default prefetch=false for int4 until we have region-based tuning, 3) set kv_eviction_policy conservative in model metadata.
elaine: i'll kick off evals: 1k instruction-following samples + 1k summarization. we need rouge-L + hallucination metric vs fp16 baseline.
sasha: small note: theres a staging tweak that worked on g-ml-12: temporarily increase KV compactor frequency (30s -> 12s) during the onboarding window; that reduced the small-chunk backlog. CPU cost increased a bit, but it's acceptable for short canaries. add that to playbook as an optional step.
ryan: also, we observed quant kernels allocate a per-request scratch buffer when prefetch=true. that buffer is ~24KB and gets freed non-contiguously. disabling prefetch removes that allocation.
maya: sample model-catalog patch I'm going to propose:
```json
{"model":"neutrino-8b-int4","defaults":{"max_new_tokens":"256","prefetch":"false","batch.max_concurrent":"6","kv_eviction_policy":"conservative"}}
```
(note: strings used in metadata to match schema)
elaine: once PR is up i'll run the extended evals in us-west1 for 48h (3k samples total) and monitor p95, evictions, and OOMs.
infra-bot: canary image built (sha: d4f2b1a), nodes labeled, traffic split 1.5%.
ryan: if we need low-latency routes, we can enable prefetch via route overrides; default remains off for stability. add route-level flag to config.
sasha: agree. add a short rollback: if OOMs > 1% in 30m window, revert to previous model or reduce concurrency.
maya: filing PR w/ load-test graphs + grafana snapshots + playbook changes. will tag owners.
elaine: ack. i'll post eval links and hallucination diffs here when ready.
ryan: :thumbsup: good catch, team.
maya: thanks all, updating thread with PR link soon. :rocket:
